selector.desc: Choose the period and generate a document with the invoice and expense detail plus the VAT/income tax summary to cross-check with your accountant.

130.desc: Advance payment of personal income tax. If you invoice companies with a 15% withholding, you may not need to file it. It's calculated as 20% of net income (income minus expenses).

303.desc: Output VAT (charged on your invoices) minus input VAT (paid on purchases and expenses). A positive result is paid to the tax authority; a negative one is offset.

111.desc: If you have employees or pay professionals subject to withholding, you must settle the withholdings applied.

100.desc: Filed between April and June of the following year. It includes all income from economic activity for the year.

390.desc: Summary of all quarterly Form 303 filings. Filed in January of the following year.

tickets.desc: Materials, fuel, tools, work clothing, phone (50%), on-site meal allowances. Without a receipt, it isn't deductible.

despacho.desc: If you use part of your home for work, you can deduct a proportional % of utilities (electricity, internet). Check the percentage with your accountant.

vehiculo.desc: If you have a vehicle used exclusively for work (a work van) you deduct 100%. A personal car: only if used exclusively for professional purposes.

telefono.desc: Phone, computer, software: 100% deductible if used exclusively for work, 50% if mixed use.

tarifaPlana.desc: First 12 months: reduced flat fee. Extendable for another 12 months if income doesn't exceed the minimum wage. Plan the timing of your registration carefully.

ivaReformas.desc: Reduced 10% rate for renovation of private homes over 2 years old. General 21% rate for commercial premises and new builds.

legislacion.title: Legislation
legislacion.subtitle: Legal framework for home and commercial renovations across Spain

selector.label: Your autonomous community
selector.desc: Select your region to see the specific urban planning regulations that apply

ccaa.obraMenorDesc: Simplified process — no structure or facade involved
ccaa.obraMayorDesc: Requires a technical project and longer timelines

legislacion.avisoText: Urban planning regulations change frequently. Always check with the relevant Town Hall and a qualified professional (architect or building surveyor) if in doubt. Conditions may vary by municipality even within the same region.

obraMenor.titulo: Minor works / Prior notice or Responsible Declaration
obraMenor.desc: Works that do not affect the structure, facade, or shared elements. The exact name and threshold vary by region and municipality — select your region to see the details.

obraMayor.desc: When the structure or facade is affected, there is a change of use, or the surface area is significant. Requires a project signed by a qualified professional (architect or building surveyor, depending on the case).
incluye: Change of use from commercial to residential
Legalization of works carried out without a permit

obrasComunidades.desc: Any work affecting shared elements requires approval from the Homeowners' Association under the Horizontal Property Act (Law 49/1960). The required quorum varies depending on the type of action.

rd1627.desc: Applies throughout Spain. For works with a project, a Health and Safety Coordinator must be appointed. For works without a project, the obligations fall on the contractor.
incluye: Prior notice to the Labor Authority
Health and Safety Plan (works >500 m² or >30 days)
H&S Coordinator on works with multiple contractors

epi.desc: Royal Decree 773/1997 requires providing and using PPE appropriate to the risk. Non-compliance can lead to serious penalties and civil or criminal liability.
incluye: Harness and lifeline for work at height
Face mask for dust or fiber work

cte.desc: National regulatory framework establishing the basic quality requirements for buildings and their installations. Applies especially to full renovations and changes of use.
incluye: DB-SUA: Safety of use and accessibility

rebt.desc: Any new or modified electrical installation must comply with the REBT. Requires an installer authorized by the region and an installation certificate for processing with the utility company.
incluye: Electrician with a valid qualification card
Registration with the competent regional authority
Mandatory inspection for installations of a certain size

rite.desc: Regulates the design, sizing, installation, maintenance and inspection of heating, air conditioning, domestic hot water and ventilation systems.
incluye: Project or technical report depending on power output
Installation certificate to commission the system

loe.desc: Defines the parties involved in construction, their obligations, and the guarantees of the construction process. Essential for understanding liabilities and warranty periods.
incluye: Mandatory ten-year insurance on new-build housing
Joint liability of the parties involved

contratoObra.desc: The Civil Code regulates works contracts throughout Spain (arts. 1588–1600). It protects both parties. It should detail the work, materials, timelines, prices, and conditions for changes.
incluye: Detailed description of work and materials

rgpd.desc: The General Data Protection Regulation (EU 2016/679) and the LOPDGDD (Organic Law 3/2018) regulate the processing of customers' personal data throughout Spain.
incluye: Information clause in quotes and contracts
Privacy policy if you have a website or app
No sharing data with third parties without consent
Right to erasure and access for data subjects

facturacion.titulo: Invoicing and obligations as a self-employed professional
facturacion.desc: As a self-employed worker (RETA), you must issue an invoice for every job, file VAT quarterly (Form 303) and personal income tax (Form 130 or withholdings). The anti-fraud law requires approved invoicing software since 2025.
incluye: Registration for business tax (IAE, heading 501–505 depending on activity)
Invoicing with all legally required elements
Keep invoices for 4 years (income tax) / 10 years (commercial)

andalucia.ley: Law 7/2021 LISTA (Law for the Promotion of Territorial Sustainability)
andalucia.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Andalusia (Department of Public Works)
andalucia.notas: LISTA simplified the permitting system. Many works previously requiring a permit now only require a self-declaration. Each municipality adapts the system through its own bylaws. Specially protected areas (coastline, historic centers) have additional requirements.

aragon.ley: Legislative Decree 1/2014 — Urban Planning Law of Aragon (LUArg)
aragon.organismo: Town Hall + Government of Aragon (Department of Territorial Structuring)
aragon.notas: In the capital, Zaragoza, the Municipal Building Bylaw applies. Prior notice applies to minor works. Heritage protection zones require a prior report from Aragon's Cultural Heritage authority.

asturias.organismo: Town Hall + Principality of Asturias (Department of Land Planning)
asturias.notas: The Asturian coastline and inland mountain areas have specific restrictions. The historic centers of Oviedo, Gijón and Avilés require additional processing with the Department of Culture.

baleares.ley: Law 12/2017 — Urban Planning of the Balearic Islands (LUIB)
baleares.organismo: Town Hall + Government of the Balearic Islands (Department of Environment and Territory)
baleares.notas: The LUIB distinguishes between interventions in consolidated urban land and protected areas. The Island Councils (Mallorca, Menorca, Eivissa, Formentera) have their own urban planning powers. Special attention to coastal zones and tourist intensification areas.

canarias.ley: Law 4/2017 — Land and Protected Natural Areas (LSENPC)
canarias.organismo: Town Hall + Government of the Canary Islands (Department of Ecological Transition)
canarias.notas: The archipelago has specific regulations due to its island nature and natural areas (Canary Islands Network of Natural Areas). Island councils (cabildos) have their own powers. Special restrictions apply in coastal and tourist areas.

cantabria.ley: Law 2/2001 — Territorial Planning and Land Urban Regime (LOTRUS)
cantabria.organismo: Town Hall + Government of Cantabria (Department of Public Works)
cantabria.notas: The Coastal Law has a particular impact on the Cantabrian coastline. Inland municipalities with ethnographic and natural heritage may require additional sector reports.

castilla-la-mancha.ley: Legislative Decree 1/2023 — Consolidated Text of the Land Planning Law
castilla-la-mancha.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Castilla-La Mancha (Department of Public Works)
castilla-la-mancha.notas: The regulation clearly distinguishes between acts requiring a permit and acts requiring a self-declaration. Historic-artistic sites (Toledo, Cuenca...) have a special regime from the Department of Culture.

castilla-leon.ley: Law 5/1999 — Urban Planning of Castilla y León (LUCyL) and amendments
castilla-leon.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Castilla y León (Department of Environment, Housing and Land Planning)
castilla-leon.notas: A vast region with a wide variety of situations. Cities with historic centers declared as Assets of Cultural Interest (Ávila, Segovia, Salamanca, Burgos, León...) require a prior report from the Directorate General of Cultural Heritage. Rural areas have specific land-use rules.

cataluna.ley: Legislative Decree 1/2010 — Catalonia Urban Planning Law (LUC)
cataluna.organismo: Town Hall + Government of Catalonia (Department of Territory)
cataluna.notas: Barcelona city has its own Metropolitan Building Bylaw and the regulations of the Metropolitan Area (AMB). Work in the Gothic Quarter or in listed buildings requires Cultural Heritage authorization. The Housing Improvement Plan (PMH) offers specific grants for renovations.

extremadura.ley: Law 15/2001 — Land and Territorial Planning of Extremadura (LESOTEX)
extremadura.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Extremadura (Department of Land Planning)
extremadura.notas: Natural heritage (Monfragüe National Park, Cornalvo Natural Park...) and cultural heritage (Mérida, Cáceres, Trujillo with protected historic sites) play a major role in shaping works in affected areas.

galicia.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Galicia (Department of Environment, Territory and Housing)
galicia.notas: The LSG has a special regime for "rural settlements" and buildings on rustic land. Santiago de Compostela, as a World Heritage city, has a Special Protection Plan for its historic center. The Coastal Law heavily affects the Galician coastline.

madrid.ley: Law 9/2001 — Land Law of the Community of Madrid (LSCM)
madrid.organismo: Town Hall + Community of Madrid (Department of Housing and Local Administration)
madrid.notas: In the municipality of Madrid, the General Urban Development Plan (PGOU) applies. Prior notice allows works to start immediately. Listed buildings and special protection areas require reports from the Project Supervision Office. Central districts (Centro, Salamanca, Chamberí) have urban landscape protection rules.

murcia.ley: Legislative Decree 1/2005 — Land Law of the Region of Murcia (LSRM)
murcia.organismo: Town Hall + Regional Government of Murcia (Department of Tourism, Culture and Environment)
murcia.notas: The Mar Menor lagoon and the Murcian coastline have specific protection legislation. Cartagena and Lorca have archaeological sites that affect works in their surroundings. Municipal bylaws vary significantly between the coast and the inland areas.

navarra.ley: Regional Law 5/2015 — Land and Urban Planning (LFOTU)
navarra.organismo: Town Hall + Government of Navarre (Department of Land Planning)
navarra.notas: Navarre has its own charter ("fuero") granting it special fiscal and regulatory powers. The Camino de Santiago pilgrim route crosses the region, creating specific protection zones. The Bardenas Reales protected natural area affects works in neighboring municipalities.

pais-vasco.ley: Law 2/2006 — Land and Urban Planning of the Basque Country (LSPV)
pais-vasco.organismo: Udala (Town Hall) + Basque Government (Department of Land Planning)
pais-vasco.notas: The Basque Country has its own economic agreement with a distinct tax regime. The General Assemblies of the three Historic Territories (Álava, Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa) have their own regulatory powers. Basque industrial heritage is specially protected. Bilbao, San Sebastián and Vitoria-Gasteiz have general plans with specific rules.

la-rioja.ley: Law 5/2006 — Land and Urban Planning of La Rioja (LOTUR)
la-rioja.organismo: Town Hall + Government of La Rioja (Department of Public Works)
la-rioja.notas: A small region with relatively simplified regulations. Logroño and the wine-producing municipalities along the Camino de Santiago have specially protected areas. Wine cellars, as a distinctive building type, have their own regulations in Designation of Origin zones.

valencia.ley: Law 5/2014 — Land Planning, Urban Planning and Landscape (LOTUP)
valencia.organismo: Town Hall + Valencian Regional Government (Department of Territory)
valencia.notas: The LOTUP incorporates environmental and landscape assessment into the urban planning process. The Valencian coastline (PATIVEL) has special protection. Valencia city has its own General Plan. Flood-prone areas (ZP or ZFC) affect works on ground floors, basements and elements in contact with the ground.

notas: • This recovers/updates the records from the backup — it doesn't delete anything you created afterwards.
• If a record from the backup no longer exists (you deleted it), it's recreated with its original data.
• Documents only restore their record (name, category, link); if the file was also deleted from storage, the link won't work.
